summary: Yoshimi Nozawa works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. As of 2026, Nozawa has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a historian and Japanologist who studied at Komazawa, Meiji, and Tezukayama universities. He was an assistant professor at Yamagata Prefectural Yonezawa Women's Junior College, president of Koshien Junior College, and a professor at Ryukoku University.

Yoshinobu Sakade (1934–2020) was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and under Mitsuji Fukunaga, later holding a position at Kansai University from around 1970 to 2005.

Yoshinori Takeuchi (1913–2002) studied philosophy and religious and Buddhist studies at Kyoto University under Hajime Tanabe. He served as an assistant professor and professor at Kyoto University, professor at Aichi Gakuin University, and member of the Japan Academy.

Yoshio Kawakatsu (1922–1984) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Kyoto University and under Paul Demiéville. He worked as a library-track assistant at Kyoto University from around 1948 until 1984.
Yoshio Nishiguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yoshitaka Iriya and Seizan Yanagida.
Yoshio Takeuchi (1886–1966) specialized in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1907 to 1910 and held a post at Tohoku University from approximately 1923 to 1946.

Yoshiro Imaeda is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. He held positions at CNRS (1974–2012), the National Library of Bhutan, and Kyoto University.

Yoshiro Tamura (1921–1989) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University. He held professorships at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo, Rissho University, and the University of Chicago.

Yoshitaka Iriya (1910–1998) studied Sinology at Kyoto University under Takeshiro Kuraishi. He held academic posts at Kyoto University, headed the Department of Chinese Literature at Nagoya University, and was a professor at Kyoto Sangyo University.

Yoshito S. Hakeda (1924–1983) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served on the faculty at Columbia University, where he was a professor and an associate professor in East Asian Languages and Cultures and Religion.
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Ohara held a post at Kyoto University attested in 2006 and a post at Kyoto National Museum attested in 2016.

Yoshitsugu Sawai is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Tenri, Tohoku, and Harvard universities under John B. Carman, among others. He was a professor and Dean of the Faculty of Humanities at Tenri University (1984–2022).

Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held positions at Taisho University as a researcher, specially appointed lecturer, and instructor, as well as a visiting post at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yoshiyuki Kawazoe earned his doctorate at Tohoku University, working there from 1975 to 2012 as an assistant and later senior research fellow. He also held professorships at JAIST and the National Institute of Informatics, specializing in computational studies and Tibetology.

Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University. He served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1957 to 1986 and director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held positions at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and Rowan University.
Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a scholar of philosophy and Sinology. He founded the Wanmu Caotang academy in 1890 and held a post there from around 1891 to 1898.

Yozo Taniyama is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University from 1991 to 2002. He held posts at Tohoku University, Shitennoji University, St. Thomas University, Japan, and Sophia University.
Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, studying under doctoral supervisors Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, as well as teacher Eric Kvan.
